newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korean 3-year yields close at 1997 low.
newsitem.headline: South Korean 3-year yields close at 1997 low.

text.p: Yields on three-year benchmark corporate bonds closed at yearly low of 11.85 percent on Tuesday thanks to abundant liquidity, brokers said.
The yields have previously reached the same 1997 low level on January 20, they said.
* Overnight average call rates at 11.67 vs 11.70
But the central bank's redemption of repurchase agreements in the afternoon pumped cash into the market, pulling the yields lower.
Fewer new issues of 21.5 billion won on Tuesday against 171 billion on Monday and a slower corporate fund demand also helped boost the sentiment.
"The corporate bond yields could drop further to 11.75 percent on Wednesday or Thursday," said a local broker.
Three-month certificate of deposit (CD) yields and overnight call rates also dropped on abundant liquidity conditions.
